questions.text: What is the register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: ID 0x00 RO, TYPE 0x04 RW, STATUS 0x08 RW, SEQ 0x0C RW, PAYLOAD 0x10 WO, BUILD 0x14 WO, INDEX 0x18 RW, BYTE 0x1C RO, LENGTH 0x20 RO, COUNT 0x24 RO, STATUSWORD 0x28 RO, all reset 0 except ID
questions.reason: The request names registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
STATUS: offset 0x01, RW, reset 0: [7:0]
PBYTE: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: [7:0] appended to the payload (24 at most); reads 0
PLEN: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: payload bytes held
IDX: offset 0x05, RW, reset 0: [6:0] position
SEQ: offset 0x02, RW, reset 0: [15:0]
STAT: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [0] building, [1] payload overflow
BUILD: offset 0x04, WO, reset 0: any write builds the reply; reads 0
LEN: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: reply length in bytes
TYPE: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [6:0] reply type (sent with bit 7 set)
BYTE: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: reply byte at IDX, 0 past the end
unmapped: reads of unused offsets give 0; writes to unused or read-only offsets do nothing

questions.text: What values are used for TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: The request says the parameters exist but not their values.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not the proposed 1000000. The specification gives no value for BUILD_STAMP, so its value is not specified and the proposed default of 0 is not supported.

questions.text: Is the reply built from the TYPE, STATUS and SEQ values at the time of the BUILD write?
questions.default: Yes, values are captured at the BUILD write.
questions.reason: Ambiguous if registers change during the up-to-64-clock build.
questions.answer: Yes, values are captured at the BUILD write.

questions.text: What happens to PAYLOAD writes or a second BUILD while building?
Does the overflow flag clear only on build or also by other means?
questions.default: Only on build completion and reset.
questions.reason: The request names only build as the clearing event.
questions.answer: The overflow flag clears on a build (the reply layout clears the payload and the overflow flag) and on reset (CPU_RESETN). The specification names no other clearing means. The proposed default's 'only' is supported by that list, not stated outright.
questions.evidence: effect: TYPE, STATUS, SEQ, payload count, overflow, reply length and index 0; no reply

questions.text: What does INDEX hold when written above 255 or a wider value?
Does a build with zero payload bytes produce a reply?
questions.answer: Yes. Any write to BUILD builds the reply, and the frame is laid out as header, PLEN, payload, CRC regardless of payload size. With zero payload bytes, PLEN is 0 and the reply is 9 bytes (1 type + 1 status + 2 SEQ + 1 PLEN + 0 payload + 4 CRC). The spec does not state the 9-byte total explicitly; it follows from the frame layout.
questions.evidence: Reply = (0x80 | TYPE), STATUS, SEQ high, SEQ low, PLEN, payload, CRC-32 (Ethernet, low byte first) of all bytes before it.
